svg.title: BranchBook in AWS
svg.desc: What BranchBook has in AWS: two environments, staging and production, in one account, and the account-level stacks around them; everything drawn is built. Outside AWS, along the top: a customer's browser, which needs no sign-in; GitHub, with two environments: staging, which admits main only, and production, which admits main only and needs an approval; and the administrator, who signs in with aws login and deploys by hand. The AWS account, whose ID is never committed. Route 53, global: the hosted zone branchbook.click, with the records branchbook.click for production and stg.branchbook.click for staging, each an alias that the environment's App stack writes. In us-east-1 (N. Virginia): the stack BranchbookAccount, built by the administrator by hand, holds the IAM OIDC provider for GitHub Actions, the IAM roles, one deploy role per GitHub environment (branchbook-github-deploy-staging and branchbook-github-deploy-production), and the AWS Budgets monthly budget, which e-mails alerts; beside it the CDK bootstrap CDKToolkit, qualifier hnb659fds. In af-south-1 (Cape Town): two environment cards, staging behind production, built from the same three stacks. The staging card is at stg.branchbook.click, with the stacks BranchbookStagingData, BranchbookStagingApp and BranchbookStagingRelease, deployed first. The production card is at branchbook.click, deployed after approval. Its stack BranchbookApp, built by the pipeline, holds AWS WAF, with a CAPTCHA on every booking and cancellation and per-address limits on bookings, lookups and all requests, ahead of AWS's managed rule groups; the Application Load Balancer, HTTPS with an ACM certificate; ECS Fargate, two or more autoscaled ARM64 tasks serving port 8080, health-checked at /readyz, in private app subnets with no public IP; the migration task, which runs Flyway once per image digest with the master secret before the service is updated; CloudWatch alarms, a dashboard, a Synthetics canary and logs; and AWS FIS experiments that stop a task or fail the database over. Its stack BranchbookData holds the VPC across two zones, with private app subnets and two NAT gateways, one per zone; Secrets Manager, holding the master database secret, which only the migration task receives, and the SMS daily cap's key; and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17, Multi-AZ, which the tasks sign in to as branchbook_app with IAM authentication over TLS, so the app has no database password. Its stack BranchbookRelease holds two SSM parameters, the deployed commit and image digest. Shared, on the right: the stack BranchbookRegistry, built by the pipeline, holding the ECR repository branchbook, with immutable tags, scanned on push; AWS End User Messaging SMS, which production alone uses, to South African numbers only, through the App stack's protect configuration; a note that staging, unlike production, has a Single-AZ database and one NAT gateway, sends simulated SMS to the demo numbers only, lets the pipeline's synthetic traffic skip the CAPTCHA with a token kept in Secrets Manager, and runs only the stop-a-task experiment; the stack BranchbookGuardrails, built by the administrator by hand, holding CloudTrail, GuardDuty, AWS Config, Security Hub and IAM Access Analyzer, the CDK execution policies and the permissions boundary; and the CDK bootstraps CDKToolkit (hnb659fds, production) and CDKToolkitStaging (bbstg, staging). The main path is a customer's request: from the browser over HTTPS to Route 53, then AWS WAF, the load balancer, a Fargate task, and RDS on port 5432 over TLS with full certificate checking. A second edge leads from Route 53 to the staging card. A flow from the Fargate task sends SMS through AWS End User Messaging. Step A: the administrator deploys BranchbookAccount, BranchbookGuardrails and the bootstraps by hand. Step 1: a delivery job signs in through OpenID Connect as its GitHub environment's deploy role, with no stored keys. Step 2: the pipeline pushes the image once to the registry; both environments run it by digest. Step 3: the pipeline deploys staging, then, after approval, production, each through its own bootstrap. Legend: Built; Main path; AWS category: compute and containers, database, networking, security, management and integration, storage and cost.

g.text: SSM parameters: the deployed commit and image digest
synthetic traffic may skip the CAPTCHA
FIS stops a task; no failover
